level: L1 interval calibration under paper drift (UP-27)

design.scheme: doi (GroupKFold, 5 folds) for the cross-conformal arms; publication-year blocks for the rolling arms
design.weight_model: LogisticRegression(C=1.0) on standardised paper meta-features, labels = test-paper vs calibration-paper, clipped to [0.05, 20]
design.best_arm_rule: narrowest arm with coverage >= 0.90; else highest coverage

kill.rule: best arm width > 2.00 or coverage < 0.88 closes the conformal line

caveats: The density ratio is estimated from the same rows it reweights. With ~1,400 calibration papers and a 23-dimensional design this is stable, but the AUC is reported so the reader can see how separable the populations are; a high AUC means the weights are doing real work, a low one means the arm collapses to the unweighted path by construction.

Weighted conformal guarantees coverage under covariate shift only. If the paper offset is a label shift -- the same compounds measured on a different scale -- the likelihood ratio is not identified from x, and no reweighting fixes it. The per-year curve is the diagnostic that separates the two.
The rolling protocol is a second layer of calibration on top of DOI-fold OOF quantiles, so its intervals are not directly comparable in width to the cross-conformal arms; online_global is the bridge.
Publication year is missing for a minority of rows; those rows are assigned the median year, which puts them in the middle of the stream rather than at an end.
ACI's gamma is selected per seed on the calibration segment, not on the test segment, but the three values are all reported so the reader can see the sensitivity.
